ios.desc:
How many hours of your day are truly yours?

oh my hours draws each hour of your day as a single mark: yours if you stayed off the apps you chose as distractions, lost if you didn't. Your whole year fits on one screen, one mark per day.

It's not a screen time report. It asks a different question: how many hours stayed distraction free today?

How it works
1. Pick the apps and categories that distract you.
2. Go about your day. A single second in one of them puts that hour on the line.
3. Checkpoint appears. Keep the hour by closing the app, or continue and lose it.
4. Choose your day limit. Too many lost hours and the day is lost too.

Four views of your time
• Day. 24 hours, one glance.
• Week. Seven days, side by side.
• Month. Four weeks in one look.
• Year. Your whole year, on one screen.

Widgets for where you actually look
Home screen and lock screen widgets, in every size, for every view. Put your grid in front of yourself, not behind another tap.

Share what you see
A single tap turns any view into a clean image. Post it, save it, or send it to a friend.

Private by design
Everything stays on your device. No account. No server. No analytics. Export your full history to CSV, anytime, free.

Not a blocker
oh my hours won't lock you out or shame you into stopping. At your hour limit, checkpoint shows up with two options: keep the hour by closing the app, or continue and lose it. Continuing is always allowed. You can switch checkpoint off

Free and Full
Free, forever: day and week views, basic widgets, the default icon set, full data export.

Full Version unlocks month and year views, their widgets, and more icon sets. One yearly payment or a one-time purchase.

About the name
It's what you'll say the first time you look at the grid.
